results.Problem: Choice A overstates routine post-administration communication to the prescriber as required. Current DCP 19-2-105 strongly encourages pharmacists/interns to send administration records to the prescriber as soon after administration as practical; the circular separately imposes mandatory timing for adverse-event communication. The linked MA-MH-SUD-ADMIN rule summary also uses overbroad required communication language and should be narrowed.
results.Proposed_Answer: D, E under the frozen wording. After the proposed wording repair to A, A, D, E.

results.Problem: Choice B and the shared FED-OUD-OTP rule record retain the obsolete one-day-at-a-time version of 21 CFR 1306.07(b). Current federal law permits a practitioner who is not separately registered as an OTP to dispense, but not prescribe, not more than a three-day supply at one time while arrangements for referral are made; the emergency treatment may not be renewed or extended.
results.Proposed_Answer: A, C, D under the frozen choices. After repair, A, B, C, D if B states the current three-day-at-one-time limit and C is clarified as the no-renewal/no-extension rule.
results.Proposed_Explanation: The pathway is a narrow practitioner-dispensing exception, not a prescription pathway. The frozen one-day-at-a-time limit is stale after the federal amendment implemented in current 21 CFR 1306.07(b).
results.Proposed_Rewrite: Replace B with: “Not more than a three-day supply may be dispensed at one time while referral arrangements are being made.” Replace C with: “The emergency treatment under this provision may not be renewed or extended.”
